If you were to weigh the Earth, would you weigh it in its own gravity, or the Sun's gravity?
Neither. You'd give its mass, which would then be adjusted to weight based on the applicable gravity.

Gravity is a force that exists between objects; the magnitude of that force is a function of the mass of each object (multiplied by a constant) and the distance between them (here's a helpful page). When we weigh ourselves, we're measuring the force of the gravitational attraction between us and Earth. We have mass, Earth has mass, but weight isn't really a property of either; it kind of exists in the space between, if that makes sense--in the interaction between the two bodies. So there is a way in which you are measuring the "weight" of the Earth every time you step on a scale (i.e. if you know your mass, how far you are from Earth's center of gravity, and the force you exert on the scale, you could, in theory and given a sufficiently precise scale, be able to calculate the mass of the Earth).
It depends on which weight the asker wants. I would go ahead and use its own gravity because that's the case with other objects on Earth.

Better. More people, more opinions, more voices.

Significantly better, for a variety of reasons:

  1. Content production. A lot of subs, especially the more niche ones, are literally holding on solely through the efforts of single-digit numbers of producers and powerusers; while there are more observers, it's still fundamentally unsustainable - less people trawling less content means less for users to do, which means fewer people come to the site because there's nothing to do!
  2. Subverse diversity. On the other site, the population is large enough that the diversity of communities is a running joke - "Of course that sub's a thing." Hobby groups, city-specific subs, fangroup subs; the larger a population, the larger the size of its minority groups will be, numerically. As it stands, Voat barely has enough population to keep its defaults/general subs at decent activity levels; niche subs for a lot of interests flat out don't exist or are limited to a scant few users.
  3. Content diversity. As it stands, Voat is... fairly biased in its political and ideological spectrum. As evidenced by the general frontpage of the defaults, the average Voat user is a cop-hating, feminist-bashing, anti-corporation generalist (god help me if I see one more fucking article from "The Daily Sheeple"). Echo chambers are always bad, and that's only one of the content problems - in addition to variety of worldviews (that is necessary for healthy analysis and discussion), there's a lack of variety in interests. Related to the above, there just flat out isn't a large population of, say, paintballers on Voat - /v/paintball has 26 subs and four posts by 3 people. The type of content that people can come to Voat for - whether it's funny gifs, or news, or cat videos - is very narrow, and that can only be fixed by having a larger population and a larger spread of ideas and interests.
